headline: High: LangGraph’s writable, networked orchestration defaults can cascade into unsafe actions; LlamaFactory adds little isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest application-defined files and stdin/stdout, and its nodes may be wired by the developer to parse content as instructions. LlamaFactory has no shared channel or output surface, so direct injection is not inherent, but the pair can still be bridged through the application-defined graph state or files. This is plausible in default orchestration setups, not provably blocked.
conditions: IF the application passes untrusted text from LangGraph file/state inputs into LlamaFactory prompts or tools, injection becomes reachable.
IF a shared file or message queue is used between the two agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and schema validator on all cross-agent text.
Route only structured JSON between agents.
Reject any content containing tool directives or role markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every message.
requires-engineering: isolate shared state per agent.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph can read/write application-defined files and has broad network egress, while LlamaFactory is local-only with no filesystem or network surfaces. If sensitive graph state is stored in shared files or checkpointer storage, LangGraph can expose it through model-provider calls or developer tools. LlamaFactory is not the leak source, but it can receive leaked state if the application forwards it.
conditions: IF graph state contains secrets and is persisted in the shared checkpointer store, LangGraph can transmit them to external model providers.
IF the application forwards shared state into LlamaFactory inputs, that state becomes visible to the second agent.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared graph state.
Redact sensitive fields before any model call.
Restrict checkpointer access to the minimum service account.
requires-engineering: encrypt persisted state at rest.
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem write and network egress, but LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or network capabilities. There is no direct overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so write-write conflict is not established. The main risk is only indirect coordination failure through shared application state, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high indicators.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same application-defined files, conflict risk increases.
IF the orchestrator omits locking around shared state, concurrent updates can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Disable concurrent writes to shared state.
Add a simple lock around the checkpointer write path.
Use append-only logs for coordination.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can produce outputs that downstream nodes or tools may treat as authoritative, and its tool-use pattern is developer-wired. LlamaFactory has no built-in verification or action constraints in the profile, so if it consumes LangGraph output, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or decisions. Because the pair’s interaction is undocumented and the orchestrator is explicitly stateful, uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory consumes LangGraph-generated text without an explicit verification step, cascading error is reachable.
IF downstream automation acts on LangGraph output, incorrect facts can propagate into actions.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification gate.
Require citations or structured evidence before action.
Mark LangGraph outputs as untrusted by default.
Log and diff every downstream action against source text.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated data handling, residency, or retention commitments. LangGraph handles model provider API keys and application-defined graph state, while LlamaFactory lists no secrets or data classes. No specific compliance mismatch is evidenced, so only a low residual risk remains from unspecified deployment choices; the other agent is not cited because no cross-agent compliance flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into LangGraph graph state and sent to external model providers, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF the deployment adds a DPA or HIPAA boundary not reflected in the profiles, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared graph state.
Use a local-only model for sensitive workflows.
Document retention and deletion settings.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review.
